newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel fund to wind up due to Mideast crisis.
newsitem.headline: Israel fund to wind up due to Mideast crisis.

text.p: The Israel Growth Fund, a U.S-based fund investing in Israeli shares, will wind up in January after failing to raise enough money due to the crisis in the Middle East peace process, its manager said on Monday.
"It's being closed simply because there wasn't demand for the product," said Adam Schor, co-portfolio manager and an analyst at Chicago-based Harris Associates.
He attributed the fund's difficulties to the political situation in Israel. "I think it was a very difficult period to get people comfortable with investing in Israel," he said.

The fund was launched on March 15, just after a wave of suicide bombings in Israel claimed the lives of 59 people. They were followed by "Operation Grapes of Wrath", Israel's air-and-artillery bombardment of Lebanon, and later the election of Israel's right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"All of this made people reluctant to invest in Israel and to overlook a compelling investment case," Schor said.

Harris managed the open-ended mutual fund for New England Life Insurance Co, which is controlled by Metropolitan Life Insurance Co. The fund was marketed to members of B'nai B'rith, the Jewish fraternal organisation.
The Israel Growth Fund had raised about $11.5 million in the nine months since it was launched, which was too little to justify management costs.
"We never had an exact goal (for the total amount to be raised), but clearly we wanted more than $11.5 million," Schor said.
The fund, which was 75 percent invested in Tel Aviv-traded stocks and about 15 percent in U.S.-traded Israeli companies, had a 4.4 percent return in dollar terms as of December 13.
In spite of the fund's failure, Schor said he remains keen on Israeli stocks as Tel Aviv was one of the cheapest stock markets in the world.
"The market is not giving a lot of good companies their credit," he said.
